correctness.rationale: In split Fourier coordinates with dual S and B=I−S, the product is û(Sχ)v̂(Bχ). Right multiplication has one nonzero row per χ with v̂(Bχ)≠0, with distinct pivot columns; left multiplication has disjoint column supports indexed by the fibers of B. Thus the two exponents count nonzero points on H=im B and occupied cosets of K=ker B, respectively. Each coset meeting H contains j=|H∩K|=p^d such points, in precisely p^(h−d) cosets. Counting zero assignments separately gives both displayed factors, both marginals and the coefficient p^h(q−1)q^(t−j), strictly distinguishing d at fixed p,m,h,q. The ranks of B and B² equal their primal counterparts; rank-nullity on H and the eigenvalue-one Jordan chains give the claimed interpretations. For h=0 there is one coset and one observed point; for h=m each coset is a singleton meeting H. The binary examples give (h,d)=(2,1) and (2,0), hence 8 and 24. The source's binary F3 census is recorded finite evidence only, and its scripts were inspected, not executed. Independent replay: python /workspace/reproductions/frozen_checks.py; the fifth check compared original-basis matrix ranks for every one of the 512 support shapes for p=3,q=7,h=d=1. No claim is made for nonsplit/modular fields or non-elementary groups.

value.rationale: The same-element joint rank spectrum measures how the two annihilator dimensions interact and is a natural refinement of separate zero-divisor counts. It does not merely report another field or numerical stratum: it yields an infinite-family classification by a kernel–image invariant independently visible in a single joint coefficient. The equal-marginal eight-dimensional examples explicitly show the precise information lost by all one-sided counts.
